gaps.quote: Every rational $M$ factors as $M=F_1\Pi F_2$, where $F_1$ and $F_2$ are lower-triangular rational matrices.
gaps.note: The page then uses F_1^{-1} and F_2^{-1}, which exist only if the factors are invertible, but lower-triangular alone does not give that (a zero diagonal entry is allowed). Paper Lemma lower-lower (line 1364-1371) requires E_1,E_2 to be invertible lower triangular.

gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: This does not follow from 'q must not divide xi' for each entry being read; it is a separate choice of q. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear proof, around line 1415-1420) picks q odd avoiding every denominator in the table of factors and inverses and the numerators of the diagonal entries of the invertible factors (for example q larger than all nonzero numerators and denominators), done once independent of b. The page never says how such a fixed q is found or why it makes the factors invertible mod q^b.

The identity and the inequality N>2L_b are only cited; the page does not say what edge matrices are or why their ranks equal the dimension changes (paper lines 1148-1167), so the reader cannot check that s_b<W_bR.
